name: Eleven-State Contraction Reduction
statement: Let $G$ be a closed-orientable, five-dimensional partial cube with an antipodal pair, no learning-space root, and at most eleven vertices. If some $\Theta$-class contraction is nonlearning, then $G$ has eleven vertices and is exactly one of three graphs: $\mathcal V_4$ with a pendant at an antipodal endpoint, or $\mathcal Z_4$ with a pendant at a degree-two or degree-three antipodal endpoint. Conversely, all three graphs satisfy these properties.
proof: The contracted antipodal graph is one of $\mathcal V_4,\mathcal Z_4,\mathcal T_4$ by the dimension-four trichotomy. Vertex counting excludes $\mathcal T_4$ and forces a singleton contracted edge class over a ten-vertex core. Since both remaining cores are 2-connected, the inverse expansion must attach a pendant at an antipodal endpoint. Their automorphism orbits give exactly the three stated types; the pendant-antipode construction proves the converse.
